$comment: tudouni configuration. Read this once, top to bottom, before editing.
QUICK START (the minimum to get a working session)
1. Pick one route under `providers` below (or add your own) and paste your
key into its `api_key`. Nothing else is required.
2. Make sure that route's `models` lists at least one model id the endpoint
actually serves.
3. Move the route you want as the default to the top of `providers`.
4. Delete the example routes, sections and keys you do not use. A route left
with an empty api_key is reported at start-up but does not stop it.
5. Start the program. If something is wrong it stops with a message that
names the file, the section and the key.
WHERE THIS FILE LIVES
The file that takes effect is ~/.tudouni/config.json (on Windows
%USERPROFILE%\.tudouni\config.json). It is created from a built-in template
the first time a missing key is reported, and it is never overwritten after
that. **It follows the person**: moving to another directory to work does
not change your keys.
**This file is the only source of configuration**: keys are not read from
environment variables or .env. The single exception is AGENT_CONFIG_FILE,
which names a different file to read instead of this one (it must exist).
GENERAL RULES
- This is strict JSON: double quotes, no trailing commas, no // comments.
- Any key starting with `$` (like this `$comment`) is a comment and is
ignored, in every section. Use it to leave notes next to a route.
- Any other key the program does not know is an **error**, not a shrug: a
misspelled key that silently does nothing is the worst kind of failure.
- Top-level keys: providers, web, image_generation, subagents. (`ui` is
accepted for old files and does nothing.)
- This file holds secrets. Do not commit it or paste it into a chat.
providers: the chat model routes
**The key is the route name** (any name you like; it is what /model and
subagents refer to). The order is the order of the /model list, and it
decides the default: the first route that has an api_key is the default.
Route keys:
base_url       REQUIRED. Where requests go, e.g. https://api.deepseek.com
api_key        The key, written right here (there is no second way).
Empty means the route is listed but cannot be used.
models         The models on this route (see below). Omit it and the
route cannot be selected.
display_name   Optional. The name shown for the route in lists; defaults
to the route name.
api_style      Optional. Which wire protocol the endpoint speaks:
openai      POST base_url/chat/completions   (default)
anthropic   POST base_url/v1/messages  (Claude, and the
Anthropic-compatible endpoints of MiniMax,
Qwen, ...)
responses   POST base_url/v1/responses
Omit it and it is worked out from base_url, which is right
for almost every route: a base_url ending in /messages,
/v1/messages or /anthropic means anthropic. Nothing else
is adjusted, so for the anthropic and responses styles
base_url must NOT already end in /v1 (the /v1 is added).
For the openai style, include /v1 yourself if the endpoint
needs it, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1
headers        Optional. Extra request headers sent on every request to
this route, as string values. For vendors that require a
custom User-Agent or a session header. Write ${session}
inside a value and it is replaced with the conversation id.
They cannot replace Authorization or Content-Type.
verify         Optional, true by default. false turns OFF TLS certificate
checks for this route. Only for an internal endpoint with a
self-signed certificate; never for a public one.
effort_levels  Optional. The thinking levels every model on this route
accepts (see THINKING LEVELS). A model can override it.
Model keys (each entry in `models`):
id                REQUIRED. The model name sent to the endpoint, exactly
as the vendor spells it. Unique within the route.
context_window    Optional. The context size in tokens (a positive whole
number). If you do not know it, delete the line: the
interface then reports usage without a percentage. A
wrong percentage is worse than none, it gets believed.
label             Optional. A friendlier name for the /model list.
summary, note     Optional. Short text shown next to the model in lists.
vision            Optional, false by default. true means the model can
read images: pasted pictures and rendered document pages
are sent to it. Set it only if the model really can.
reasoning_effort  Optional. The thinking level the model starts on;
`high` if omitted.
effort_levels     Optional. Overrides the route's effort_levels.
The same model id may appear on two routes (e.g. a vendor and a gateway);
it is then shown as route/model so you can tell which one bills you.
THINKING LEVELS (reasoning_effort / effort_levels)
The vocabulary is: minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max. `reasoning_effort`
on a model is the level it starts on; `effort_levels` is which levels it
accepts, and it is what /effort offers and enforces.
Leave effort_levels out and /effort offers the whole vocabulary; a level the
model does not take comes back as an error from the endpoint. That is the
deliberate default: listing too much costs one visible error, listing too
little hides a level that works. Declare effort_levels when you know better;
values are never rewritten, so what you pick is what goes on the wire.
`none` is not a level: it means thinking off, which is /thinking, not /effort.
NETWORK / PROXY
Requests follow the machine's proxy: the standard proxy environment
variables (HTTPS_PROXY and friends) if set, otherwise the system proxy, and
NO_PROXY for hosts to reach directly. /status shows which path is in use.
web: web search
tavily_api_key    Your Tavily key (https://tavily.com). Leave it empty or
delete the section and web_search is not registered.
tavily_base_url   Optional. Defaults to https://api.tavily.com
fetch_web (reading a page by URL) needs no key and always works.
image_generation: the route that draws pictures (generate_image)
Delete the whole section and generate_image is simply not registered;
nothing else changes. It is a separate section, not a `models` entry,
because an image model listed there could be picked as the chat model.
provider    The chat route (a name under `providers`) to inherit the key,
base_url and headers from, so one key is written once.
model       REQUIRED. The image model (gpt-image-1 and the like). It is
**never** inherited: the chat route's model is a different model.
api_style   Optional. Only one is implemented:
openai-images   POST base_url/images/generations
base_url / api_key / headers
Optional overrides of what was inherited. Required when there
is no `provider`. A `headers` here replaces the inherited ones.
A generation endpoint is often not the chat endpoint (some gateways serve
only one of the two), so an inherited base_url may answer 404 for
/images/generations. The error message names the URL that was used.
The picture lands in the workspace as a real file (out/poster.png): it can be
shown with ![](path), declared with present, and opened again later.
subagents: which models delegated tasks run on (optional)
Without this section a delegated task runs on the same route and model as
your session. With it you offer the main model a short menu of presets and
it picks one by name; it never invents a model name. Shape:
"subagents": {
"default": "fast",
"presets": [
{"name": "fast", "provider": "deepseek", "model": "deepseek-flash",
"effort": "low", "purpose": "search, locate, read large files"}
default    Optional. The preset used when none is named. Empty or absent
means: follow the parent session.
presets    Up to 8 entries, shown in this order. Each one:
name       REQUIRED. Letters, digits, - and _; at most 32 characters;
unique.
provider   REQUIRED. A route name under `providers`.
model      REQUIRED. A model id listed on that route.
effort     Optional. A thinking level that model accepts.
purpose    Optional but recommended. What the preset is for, in your
words. It is what the main model reads to choose.
A preset whose route has no api_key is not an error at start-up; the
delegation that tries to use it is refused with a message naming the route.

anthropic-example.$comment: An Anthropic Messages route with declared thinking levels. Note base_url has no /v1: it is added for this style.

headers-example.$comment: A route that needs its own client identification. The api_key carries the credential; these ride along with it, and neither is invented from a provider name. ${session} is replaced with the conversation id.

image_generation.$comment: Inherits the key and base_url from the deepseek route above; change provider/model to an endpoint that really serves images, or delete this whole section to turn generate_image off.
